purpose: CURRENT-STATE.json is the single place for the MicroDuck robot's CURRENT measured facts. Sim judgements, briefs and child sessions read these values from here. History (memory files, DECISIONS.md, logs, transcripts, code comments) explains how a value was reached and is never a source for the current value. When a measurement changes a fact, update its entry here in the same turn and move the old value into its 'superseded' list.
check: python3 ~/code/claude-config/scripts/state_check.py microduck-sim/CURRENT-STATE.json   (runs each probe on the newest walk_wired run; fails on a mismatch, on newer evidence it could not measure, and on any fact older than its max_age_days; sim_suite.sh runs it first and stops on failure)

imu_rate_hz.meaning: IMU samples reaching the 50 Hz policy loop per second while walking: full rate, every tick fresh.
imu_rate_hz.source: 2026-10-18 A7Z head board (J12 UART2 500 kbaud): walk-mode status lines of runs 1018a/b/d (/tmp/duck_wired_1018{a,b,d}.out, archived in guide/firmware/mac/robot-runs-20261018), median 51/s, none below 38/s
imu_rate_hz.measure: the probe reads the newest run's stdout (/tmp/duck_wired_<suffix>.out next to /tmp/duck_wired_log_<suffix>.jsonl): median of torque-on 'imu N/s' lines; at most max_low_share of lines may sit more than two tolerances below (the 10/16 brownout run 1016k had 46 %)

superseded.why: Pi Zero W CPU saturated by a stuck cloud-init; fixed by disabling cloud-init (session 鸭子步态测试准备, 10/16)

imu_added_delay_ms.meaning: No delay beyond the normal pipeline (about 15 ms end to end plus half a 50 Hz period, same as the community duck); the 40-60 ms trunk lag is plant softness, not IMU.
imu_added_delay_ms.source: stance analysis + raw-gyro test 10/15 (memory microduck-imu-latency-measured); Shawn 2026-10-15 and 2026-10-17 ('证实是没有延迟')
imu_added_delay_ms.measure: stance_switch.py analysis; not re-measured by the check (age-limited by max_age_days)

servo_read_drop_fraction.meaning: Fraction of 20 ms walk-mode ticks without a fresh servo sync read while the legs step (the policy skips those ticks and the servos hold the last goals).
servo_read_drop_fraction.source: walk_wired logs /tmp/duck_wired_log_1016{m..zb}.jsonl and 1017a.jsonl: 3.3-5.2 % of stepping-window ticks have missing servos (1017a 4.6 %, 152 ticks); recounted 2026-10-17 after the probe fix
servo_read_drop_fraction.measure: the probe reads the newest /tmp/duck_wired_log_*.jsonl: walk-mode ticks within 0.3 s of a tick whose leg joints move faster than 0.5 rad/s, counting fresh=False or missing servos

superseded.why: 10/15 sync-read misses on the Pi Zero W bus
the probe counted only ticks with an action; a tick with a dropped read runs no policy, so every dropped tick was excluded and the probe always read 0

walking_policy.value: walk61.onnx (Pollen BEST_alpha_walking, runtime-overlay/models) at 0.25 m/s, 4 s walks; KP_RL 200, stand mode KP 400
walking_policy.source: 2026-10-18 robot runs 1018d (walk61 0.25 m/s, 3 s, clean twice), guide/firmware/mac/robot-runs-20261018/README.md
candidates: runtime-overlay/models-ft3-it999 (ft3 iteration 999, D-017): sim-better; on the robot 2026-10-17 and 2026-10-18 (three walks at 0.20 m/s, guide/firmware/mac/robot-runs-20261018) it lost balance at 2.5-4 s every time, while walk61 at 0.25 m/s for 3 s walked and stopped cleanly twice
walking_policy.measure: the --models directory and --kp flags of the newest walk_wired run in the main session (its stdout header), and the walk61.onnx in that directory; Shawn's go for any change

power.value: Servo rail: USB-C PD charger at 20 V 5 A -> Adafruit 5991 -> XL4015 #1 (about 7.2 V) -> OpenRB J4. A 20 V 3 A charger crashes the A7Z while walking or standing up; 20 V 5 A walks without a crash (Shawn, 2026-10-22). A7Z: the same 20 V from the 5991 -> XL4015 #2 -> header pins 2/6 (one supply for both rails). No battery on the robot.
power.source: Shawn's swap test 2026-10-22: 3 A charger -> A7Z froze 4 times within seconds of walking/standing (watchdog HOT-BOOT 16 s later, recorder rows all stop in one instant); 5 A charger -> no stop. Mechanism: the 60 W charger cuts or folds back at the walking/stand-up current peaks, both XL4015 outputs dip together, the XL330s keep running at the lower voltage while the A7Z SoC freezes
power.measure: charger label and the 5991 display; walk/stand test with the A7Z flight recorder running (guide/firmware/pi/BLACKBOX.md). Servo-reported voltage (0.1 V steps, one servo per cycle) cannot see millisecond dips and is not evidence of a stable rail

superseded.value: 5991 bench supply at 20 V -> XL4015 #1 servo rail (no-load 7.32 V, walking min about 7.0 V) and XL4015 #2 Pi 5.16 V; no battery on the robot
superseded.why: the charger behind the 5991 decides whether the A7Z survives walking: a 20 V 3 A charger froze the A7Z four times on 10/21-10/22, a 20 V 5 A charger did not (Shawn's swap test); the 10/16 entry did not name the charger rating

servo_rail_v.meaning: Servo supply voltage while walking; sim_suite.sh passes it to brain_sim_check.py as --volt for the real cases (the sim holds the supply constant).
servo_rail_v.source: memory microduck-walk-1016-state, 10/16 afternoon walk 4: XL4015 #1 current-limit trimmer at its end, no-load 7.32 V, rail min 7.0 V while walking (1 Hz servo voltage samples)
servo_rail_v.measure: walk_wired --supply auto or battery logs the servo-reported supply (bench runs do not); not re-measured by the check (age-limited by max_age_days)

superseded.why: D-014 bench rail target 7.40 V with Shutdown 52; the suite hardcoded it
5991 at 15 V before the trimmer was turned to its end

a7z_imu_bus.value: BNO085 at 0x4A on A7Z i2c-7 (TWI7, header pin 3 SDA blue, pin 5 SCL yellow), TWI7 in engine mode via /boot/dtbo/zz-duck-twi7-engine.dtbo, listed by u-boot-update after sun60iw2p1-twi7.dtbo; imu_read.py 7 reads it
a7z_imu_bus.meaning: How the A7Z reaches the IMU. In drv mode (twi_drv_used = 1, set by Radxa's sun60iw2p1-twi7.dtbo) TWI7 wedges after boot, after zero-length writes and after reads that hit the IMU while it resets, until the driver is rebound. The engine overlay must load after Radxa's twi7 overlay; u-boot-update (run by rsetup on every overlay change) orders /boot/dtbo alphabetically, hence the zz- name.
a7z_imu_bus.source: 2026-10-18 A7Z bring-up: engine mode passed first use 19 s after boot, a zero-length write, reads during an IMU soft reset, and the unmodified imu_read.py (roll -67.5, pitch -4.2, |acc| 9.80 m/s2, robot on its side); overlay source guide/firmware/pi/duck-twi7-engine.dts; 2026-10-18 20:22 renamed to zz-, extlinux regenerated by sudo u-boot-update, rebooted: twi_mode '0: engine', i2cdetect -r 7 shows 4a, then imu_read.py 3 7 reads (roll -74.1, pitch -7.5)
a7z_imu_bus.measure: on the A7Z: cat /sys/devices/platform/soc@3000000/2517000.twi/twi_mode must say '0: engine'; python3 imu_read.py 5 7 prints orientation

superseded.value: BNO085 at 0x4A on A7Z i2c-7 (TWI7, header pin 3 SDA blue, pin 5 SCL yellow), TWI7 in engine mode via /boot/dtbo/duck-twi7-engine.dtbo; imu_read.py 7 reads it
superseded.why: Name duck- sorts before sun60iw2p1-twi7.dtbo, so the next u-boot-update (any rsetup overlay change) would have put Radxa's drv-mode overlay last

ankle_bracket.value: V1.24/V1.25 two-half ankle on both legs: the stock one-piece orange bracket cut at mid shaft, outer half on the servo horn (four M2 x 4), inner half on the V1.22 black sleeve, the halves held together only by the V1.22 slip-fit foot and the toe M2 x 6; sole material not recorded
ankle_bracket.meaning: Which ankle bracket and foot interface is on the robot. Stand behaviour depends on it: on 2026-10-21 the trunk rocked about the ankle axis with every leg encoder still on this ankle (stand_check.py), not on the 10/19 one-piece bracket with the same feet.
ankle_bracket.source: Shawn 2026-10-21: "现在装的是 V1.24/V1.25 两半踝，只靠滑配脚和脚尖螺丝夹住。" Design: guide/print/ankle-halves-20261020/README.md
ankle_bracket.measure: ask Shawn or look at the ankle: a seam across the orange bracket at mid shaft is the two-half ankle

superseded.value: stock one-piece orange bracket with the V1.22 slip-fit foot and toe M2 x 6 (all 10/19 runs)
superseded.why: replaced by the V1.22 split ankle and then the V1.24 two-half ankle (guide/print/ankle-split-20261019, ankle-halves-20261020)

a7z_touch_bus.value: XIAO ESP32-S3 at I2C 0x2A on /dev/i2c-0 = TWI0 (2510000.twi, engine mode) on A7Z header pins 29 (PB2, SCL, blue) and 31 (PB3, SDA, green), 3V3 red pin 17, GND black pin 25, from /boot/dtbo/zz-duck-twi0-touch.dtbo (source guide/firmware/pi/duck-twi0-touch.dts); a plain 24-byte read returns the block aligned (no filler byte); all five head pads (L1, R1, L2, R2, M) rise when pressed; rest counts 22100-26300
a7z_touch_bus.meaning: How the A7Z reads the head touch pads and whether each pad responds. A pad whose lead touches metal reads 0x3FFFFF and, because the firmware leaves max_meas_time_us at 0, freezes the whole touch scan. duck-telemetry.py and touch_live_a7z.py use /dev/i2c-0 when TWI0 is up and fall back to bit-banging gpiochip0 lines 34/35 otherwise (then a read costs tens of ms of CPU and pauses while a brain runs).
a7z_touch_bus.source: 2026-10-21 after installing the overlay and rebooting (uptime 25 s): i2c-0 of_node twi@2510000, twi_mode '0: engine', pinmux PB2/PB3 -> 2510000.twi twi0; 100/100 reads of 24 bytes in 2.3 s with 0.01 s CPU in total; robot monitor 611 reads 0 lost on /dev/i2c-0; IMU on i2c-7 still reads (imu_read.py 3 7). Pads: 2026-10-20 Shawn pressed each pad on the robot monitor and all five bars rose.
a7z_touch_bus.measure: on the A7Z: readlink -f /sys/bus/i2c/devices/i2c-0/of_node ends in twi@2510000; python3 touch_live_a7z.py shows five counts below 4194303 and '/dev/i2c-0'; a pressed pad rises
consumers: any duck behaviour that reacts to head touches

superseded.value: XIAO ESP32-S3 at I2C 0x2A on A7Z header pins 29 (PB2, SCL, blue) and 31 (PB3, SDA, green), 3V3 red pin 17, GND black pin 25; no kernel I2C overlay on these pins, read by bit-banging gpiochip0 lines 34/35 (duck-telemetry.py `touch`, touch_live_a7z.py) at about 8-10 reads/s; all five head pads (L1, R1, L2, R2, M) rise when pressed; rest counts 22100-26300
superseded.why: TWI0 overlay zz-duck-twi0-touch.dtbo installed; the bus is now the kernel's /dev/i2c-0, bit-banging is only the fallback

a7z_closed_head_thermal_and_resets.value: closed head, brain plus a 50 Hz policy load, bench supply: SoC 85 C after 5 min and 93 C after 9 min, both CPU clusters pinned at 416 MHz by the thermal governor (trips at 60 C), brain loop p50 23.6 ms / p90 24.6 ms (about 42 ticks/s); the board reset at about 90 C in stand61 and twice within 10 s of a walk start at 45 C and 77 C (3 resets in 25 min); no kernel thermal message (journal volatile, critical trip 110 C)
a7z_closed_head_thermal_and_resets.meaning: Whether the A7Z can run the 50 Hz brain inside the closed V1.17 head, and how the board fails there. Acceptance for staying in the head: policy-row loop p90 <= 18 ms and >= 49 ticks/s after a one-hour soak (pi/A7Z-CPU-COMPARE.md).
a7z_closed_head_thermal_and_resets.source: guide/firmware/mac/robot-runs-20261022-a7z/README.md (cpu_compare_progress.log minutes 5-9 of soak run 2, thermal.log, brain tick logs around the three resets)
a7z_closed_head_thermal_and_resets.measure: a7z_cpu_compare.py run default --head closed --soak-min 55 --burn policy_burn.py; read the minute lines and the verdict
consumers: D-021 decision on the board's place (head or torso)
any brief that quotes A7Z throttling or reset behaviour

superseded.value: 10/21 closed head, no extra load: loop p50 14.1 -> 21.8 ms and 49.9 -> 43.7 ticks/s in 12 min; 10/19 four resets after 35 min at 77-88 C
superseded.why: re-measured 2026-10-22 with the policy load; resets now seen at 45-90 C, two at walk starts

graded_hold.value: graded hold ON on the A7Z: /tmp/duck_hold.json {"on": true} with the calibration made 2026-10-23T17:16 from walk_wired run app1023-210738 (pad_lo [624.5, 698.0, 320.5, 352.0, 474.8], pad_hi [1998.4, 2233.6, 1025.6, 1126.4, 1519.2], grip_full_mm2 1010.6, legs_stand_ma 294 in stand61, legs_air_ma 138); copy kept at ~/duck-logs/hold_cal_app1023-210738.json; legs_air_ma comes from the one lift that did not struggle (struggling lifts raise the leg current to 2-2.9 A, so they cannot calibrate the unloaded level)
graded_hold.meaning: Whether walk_wired.py scales stand61/walk61's actions and softens the legs while a hand grips the head and the feet are unloaded (hold.py), and with which pad and leg-current thresholds. /tmp is cleared at every A7Z boot: after a reboot the hold is off until the copy is put back (cp ~/duck-logs/hold_cal_app1023-210738.json /tmp/duck_hold.json); the brain reads the file live, no restart.
graded_hold.source: 2026-10-23 run app1023-210738, labels ~/duck-logs/hold_labels_app1023-210738.jsonl (25 trials, segmented from the log in chat). Hold off: 4 of 5 head lifts struggled (|action| 2.1-2.3 rad, leg current peaks 2.0-2.9 A). Hold on: 6 of 6 head lifts held (s 0.00, kp_leg 80, kp_neck 500, |action| <= 0.62, leg current median 83-97 mA in the air), s back above 0.95 within 0.02-0.09 s of release, no hardware fault, mode stayed walk.
graded_hold.measure: on the A7Z: python3 -c 'import sys; sys.path.insert(0, "/home/radxa/duck"); import hold; print(hold.read_hold_file())' shows on True and the cal above; the newest duck_wired_log row has hold_on true and hold.load near 1 while standing
consumers: anyone lifting the duck by the head

sim_real_condition: The as-built suite's 'real' cases take every sensor and supply flag from these facts through robot_state_check.py --print-sim-args (--volt from servo_rail_v, IMU hold only if imu_rate_hz < 49, read drops only if servo_read_drop_fraction > 0, extra sensor delay only if imu_added_delay_ms > 0). Cases with harsher settings are 'stress' cases: report them, never accept or reject a policy on them.
